name: Jev Judgment Kernel
description: A mu-style judgment kernel for QwenPaw: at decision points on the tool seam a small fast judge (jev / TypeSafe System One protocol, any HTTP judge, a raw systemone server such as ollama's decision models, or any OpenAI-compatible chat model) answers one bounded typed question (noul/choice/score) with a calibrated probability. Verdicts cascade through judge tiers, land in a ledger, and in active mode can deny a tool call or escalate it to the human; shadow mode records without enforcing so you can read the ledger before handing a point to a judge. The agent_route point turns the same seam into an agent router: jev_route returns one agent id (or ask_human) and never calls QwenPaw itself, so the orchestrator keeps its own chat_with_agent dispatch. Reference: github.com/qybaihe/mu (docs/judges.md, docs/reference/decision-points.md).

description_i18n.zh-CN: mu 式判断内核：在工具接缝的决策点上，让一个小而快的 judge（jev / System One 协议、任意 HTTP judge 或任意 OpenAI 兼容聊天模型）回答一个有界的类型化问题（noul/choice/score），附带校准概率。裁决按 tiers 级联并写入 ledger；active 模式下可拒绝工具调用或升级给人类确认，shadow 模式只记录不拦截，便于先读 ledger 再放权。参考：github.com/qybaihe/mu。 agent_route 决策点把同一接缝变成 agent 路由器：jev_route 只返回一个 agent id（或 ask_human），自身不调用 QwenPaw，派单仍由 Orchestrator 用原生 chat_with_agent 完成；shadow 模式记录推荐与分派表的一致率。
description_i18n.en-US: mu-style judgment kernel: bounded typed questions with calibrated probabilities at tool-seam decision points, cascading judge tiers, ledger, shadow/active modes.

author: leo

meta.notes: Config: jev.json in the plugin dir (explicit override, checked first) or <host>/plugin-data/jev-kernel/jev.json (durable home that survives reinstalls); hot-reloaded by mtime; $JEV_KERNEL_CONFIG overrides both (tests). Schema mirrors mu's mu.json judge section: points (tool.risk/tool.approval/agent_route -> active|shadow|off), tiers, routes, judges (name -> {type: typesafe|http|llm|systemone, baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnv, timeoutMs}), thresholds (yes/no/minProbability/risk), agentRoute (candidates, descriptions, threshold, askMin, margin), approvalTools, skipTools, timeoutMs, recordState, stateChars. The built-in tier name 'jev' resolves mu's provider order from env keys (TYPESAFE_API_KEY, MU_JUDGE_OPENROUTER_API_KEY, AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY, OPENCODE_API_KEY, CLOUDFLARE_API_KEY+CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID) and falls back to the free OpenCode Zen tier (jev-1.13-free) when no key is set; the built-in tier name 'session' inherits the QwenPaw session's own model (agent active_model -> provider base_url + in-memory credential via ProviderManager.get_instance(), OpenAI-compatible providers only; mu's `mu setup --judge model`), sending extraBody {enable_thinking: false} with a 15s timeout because thinking models blow the judge latency budget. Defaults are inert: tool.risk=shadow (ledger only), tool.approval=off, agent_route=shadow (records agreement, dispatches nothing), tiers empty (no judge is contacted until one is configured or a provider key is exported and tiers set to ["jev"]). Ledger: <host>/plugin-data/jev-kernel/ledger.jsonl (single-generation rotation). Tools: jev_ask (bounded typed question -> calibrated verdict), jev_route (one task -> one agent id or ask_human, with shadow agreement), jev_ledger (mu ledger). No judge in time -> the point falls back to no-verdict behaviour and the ledger records why (mu's rule). Design grounding: mu docs/judges.md + docs/reference/decision-points.md; wire format verified against mu-agent 0.1.8 (packages/judge/dist/kyrn-judge.js).
